chase_cards.name: Elite Four Trainer
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is the rare top-four lane where Pokémon borrowed the in-game Elite Four idea and pinned it to real tournament players. The card is not just a rank: it is the Master League finalist apparatus made visible through photographs.

claims.text: The local catalog models Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan top 4 prize as one unnumbered promotional source row containing Elite Four Trainer at source index 256.
Bulbapedia says Elite Four Trainer was awarded to the top four ranking players of the Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan Deciding Match finals held in Tokyo on August 17, 2002.
Bulbapedia gives the card text as recognizing the Pokémon Card Game Official Tournament Battle Road Summer 2002 Master Trainers League Elite Four.
Bulbapedia says Elite Four Trainer features photographs of the top four players and is one of only a handful of Pokémon cards to feature images of real-life people.
Bulbapedia lists the qualifying regional Battle Road Summer 2002 events from July 20 through August 11, with finals in Tokyo on August 17.

Pokumon says the top four winners of the Grand Master League were crowned as the Four Heavenly Kings, known in English as the Elite Four, and that 2002 was the only year this Grand Master League structure was held.

Bulbapedia says the exact number of Elite Four Trainer cards in existence is unknown, though one copy for each winner is likely, and Pokumon lists estimated copies as 4; this is not treated as an official copy count.

Bulbapedia categorizes the card with unknown illustrators, and the attached variant references do not provide a stable row-level production credit; this tranche therefore keeps the art lane as top-four player photographs / unpromoted production design.

As judged collector texture, Elite Four Trainer matters because it translates the in-game Elite Four idea into the tournament apparatus: four real Master League players become a tiny, photograph-bearing card lineage.

Agents should preserve Elite Four Trainer / 四天王トレーナー identity, source index 256, Battle Road Summer 2002 Best in Japan top-four route, Master Trainers League context, real-player photo construction, and non-equivalence with No.1/No.2/No.3 Trainer, Worlds / World Championships, Neo Road, or generic Elite Four listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Battle Road Summer 2002 Elite Four Trainer: four real players become the myth
narrative.why_it_matters: This card is wonderfully strange. Pokémon takes one of its deepest game structures, the Elite Four, and lets four real Master League players wear it for a moment. The photographs matter because they make the myth local and bodily: four people, one finals route, one top-four card family, and a tiny uncertain population that collectors can talk around but should not overstate.

Check for the Master Trainers League / Grand Master League top-four context, not a regional podium route.
Look for the August 17, 2002 Tokyo finals context after the July-August regional circuit.
Check that the card construction features top-four real-player photographs; treat the photograph lane as core identity evidence.
Do not promote a named illustrator unless stronger row-level source evidence appears; record the art lane as player photographs / unpromoted production design.

Separate this row from Best in Japan No.1/No.2/No.3, regional Battle Road Summer trophies, Worlds / World Championships Elite Four language, Neo Road photo cards, Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle, Lizardon Mega Battle, and Kamex Mega Battle.
